headline: ESMA CSRD Priorities Focus on Supply Chains as Greenwashing Rules Take Effect
summary: ESMA has highlighted double materiality and value chain negative impacts as key 2026 CSRD enforcement priorities for listed companies. Meanwhile, new EU greenwashing regulations have taken effect, introducing severe penalties for unsubstantiated environmental claims. In response, brand owners must rigorously verify supplier sustainability data and audit consumer-facing marketing claims.

items.title: ESMA Sets 2026 CSRD Enforcement Priorities on Value Chain Impacts
items.what: ESMA has published its 2026 enforcement priorities for CSRD disclosures, emphasising double materiality and explicitly warning companies against underreporting negative value chain impacts.
items.meaning: As a listed entity in scope for CSRD, your reporting must accurately reflect environmental and labour risks within your Chinese manufacturing supply chain.
items.action: Ensure double materiality assessments cover key environmental and social risks across your Chinese supplier network.

items.title: Strict EU Anti-Greenwashing Rules Take Effect with Turnover Fines
items.what: EU rules prohibiting misleading environmental claims have reportedly taken effect, introducing potential penalties of over 4% of annual turnover for non-compliance.
items.meaning: All consumer claims regarding tool sustainability, battery platform eco-credentials, or packaging recyclability must be rigorously substantiated across EU sales channels.
items.action: Audit consumer marketing claims and packaging statements against verification requirements.

items.title: EFRAG Consults on 2027–2029 Sustainability Reporting Agenda
items.what: EFRAG launched a public consultation regarding its work programme for 2027–2029, seeking feedback on the development of future reporting standards under CSRD.
items.meaning: Emerging standards could introduce specific disclosures relevant to consumer electronics, power tool manufacturing, and product life cycles.
items.action: Monitor consultation developments to gauge future supply chain reporting requirements.

sources.title: EU CSRD: EFRAG launched consultation on its 2027–2029 sustainability reporting agenda, Julia Voskoboinikova

items.title: EU Trilogues Begin on Potential CBAM Scope Expansion
items.what: Trilogue negotiations have commenced regarding the expansion of CBAM, with EU institutions divided over whether to extend coverage to downstream finished goods.
items.meaning: While finished power tools are currently exempt, extending CBAM to downstream products could increase import compliance costs and reporting obligations.
items.action: Track trilogue outcomes regarding downstream finished product inclusion.
